title: Mathlib v4.30 source proposition Int.le.elim
statement: The proposition declared as `Int.le.elim` in the pinned Mathlib v4.30 source.

formal.statement: ∀ {a b : ℤ}, a ≤ b → ∀ {P : Prop}, (∀ (n : ℕ), a + ↑n = b → P) → P

evidence.supports: `Int.le.elim` is admitted as a Theorem with EXACTLY the stated shape, pinned verbatim via the kernel's own renderer: `((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : Int.le x0 x1) -> ((x3 : Prop) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Int (Int.add x0 (Int.ofNat x4)) x1) -> x3))) -> x3)))))`. This is the CPS elimination form of `Int.le_dest`'s `Exists` witness -- `le_dest` produces `b = a + ofNat i`, Mathlib's direction is `a + ofNat n = b`, so the equation is flipped with `isymm` before handing it to the minor premise. Declared as a child of `le` (`Int.le.elim`), the same namespacing `Nat.le.step` uses for a name under an unrelated head. Only the Exists-flavoured cousin (`Int.le_dest`) existed under any name before this -- confirmed by a shape-search returning nothing at >=0.75 for the CPS shape. Built via `Exists.elim` (ops::exists_elim) in a new file, int_prelude/order_coercion.rs.

notes: Established in Axeyum, not merely matched against Mathlib's prior statement. This is genuinely new construction, not a rename: checked hours before this lane started, the CPS elimination form `Int.le.elim` did not exist in the kernel under any name -- only the Exists-flavoured `Int.le_dest` did. Confirmed against the pinned Mathlib v4.30.0 source (commit c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f) that `Int.le.elim` is the standard CPS-style destructor of `Int.le` about the SAME `Int.le`/`Int.add`/`Int.ofNat` this kernel already has (no new definition introduced), so mirroring it is honest under the mirror-flip criterion. Preregistered in artifacts/autogenesis/nursery-v2-extension.json, which carries the partition; that manifest, not this file, is the split authority. Screened against the mirror-divergence registry and the statable-here vocabulary before preregistration.
